$comment: Time-limited, OWNED exceptions to the blocking release security gate.
The gate (scripts/audit-deps.mts --allowlist) fails the release when a
high/critical advisory is present. An entry here suppresses ONE advisory
for ONE package until its expiry date.
Rules the gate enforces mechanically, so an exception cannot rot:
- An entry past `expires` is a HARD FAILURE, not a silent pass. That is
the whole point: a 'temporary' suppression with no deadline is how a
known-vulnerable dependency ships forever.
- Every field below is REQUIRED. No anonymous, undated suppressions.
- An entry that no longer matches any live advisory is reported as stale
so it gets deleted rather than accumulating.
`package` must match the npm package name npm audit reports.
`id` is the GHSA identifier (preferred) or the npm advisory URL.
`expires` is an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), UTC. Keep it short — weeks, not
months. If you need longer, that is a decision to re-take, not extend.
`owner` is a GitHub handle who is accountable for closing it.
`reason` must say why shipping is acceptable, not merely that a fix is
unavailable — e.g. 'not reachable: pruned from the runtime image by
scripts/prune-migrate-deps.mjs'.
Example (kept out of `exceptions` on purpose — copy, do not uncomment):
"id": "GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx",
"package": "some-package",
"owner": "@gadgetusaf",
"reason": "Dev-only; not present in the runtime image. Upstream fix tracked in #123."
